project.name: ESP32 Sampler
project.goal: Implement a simple, stable v1 sampling engine optimized for real-world testing rather than maximum feature count.
design_principles: Prefer deterministic behavior over aggressive optimization.
Avoid dynamic complexity in the audio path.
Separate audio, UI, and loading responsibilities.
Load only what is required for current MIDI assignments.
Collect useful runtime metrics for future iteration.

in_scope: oldest-voice stealing when all voices are occupied
sample memory policy: RAM for short assigned samples when budget allows, otherwise stream from SD
automatic loading of saved assignments/settings on boot
separation of UI, sample loading, and audio execution contexts
dedicated CPU/core allocation strategy for audio and non-audio work
preview/browsing support through on-demand SD streaming
runtime diagnostics relevant to audio stability and memory usage

notes: Keep v1 format support narrow to reduce implementation and debugging risk.
If stereo is supported, enforce one consistent internal mixing path.

execution_domains.name: audio_engine
responsibilities: own and update the 8-voice pool
consume trigger events from a lock-safe queue
mix active voices into output buffers
read from RAM-backed sample sources
consume already-prepared stream buffers for SD-backed sources
mark voices inactive when playback ends
send completed buffers to audio output layer
must_not_do: dynamic heap allocation in steady-state audio callback
blocking SD reads in the critical mixing path

execution_domains.name: sample_loader
responsibilities: scan SD library at boot
read saved mapping/settings
build active sample set from saved MIDI assignments
read WAV headers only for active samples
classify active samples as RAM or STREAM according to policy
load RAM-assigned samples into sample memory budget
prepare and refill buffers for streamed voices
provide preview playback source data when browsing library
must_not_do: block UI unnecessarily for long operations without status feedback
reclassify RAM/STREAM policy automatically during live playback

execution_domains.name: ui_controller
responsibilities: library browsing
editing MIDI note assignments
triggering preview playback requests
showing loading and error states
initiating save of settings
displaying diagnostics relevant to v1
must_not_do: heavy synchronous SD work inside UI event handlers

rules: Use explicit queues/messages between UI, loader, and audio domains.
Avoid shared mutable state without clear ownership.
Audio domain consumes immutable or prebuilt descriptors whenever possible.
Loader domain owns file I/O and sample preparation.
UI domain requests actions but does not perform file-system or audio-critical work directly.

goals: Give audio the most predictable execution environment.
Prevent UI and SD activity from interrupting sample mixing.
Keep loader and UI on the non-audio core.

loader_task.timing: should prepare data ahead of playback needs

ui_task.timing: responsive but never at expense of audio

notes: Core numbering may be adapted to platform conventions, but audio must remain isolated on its own core/task domain.
All blocking SD and settings I/O must stay off the audio task.

principles: Do not preload the full library.
Only samples assigned to MIDI notes are candidates for playback preparation.
At boot, library discovery may store filenames/paths for browsing, but detailed audio preparation is limited to assigned samples.
Sample RAM has a fixed configurable budget separate from audio working memory.
No dynamic memory churn in the steady-state audio path.

memory_regions.name: sample_ram_pool
contents: fully loaded assigned samples classified as RAM

memory_regions.name: stream_buffer_pool
contents: read-ahead buffers for streamed active voices

policy_description: Only MIDI-assigned samples are evaluated for preload/stream decisions.
If assigned sample duration is <= preload_threshold_seconds and sample RAM budget permits, load full sample to RAM.
If sample does not fit in remaining sample RAM budget, classify it as STREAM.
If assigned sample duration is > preload_threshold_seconds, classify it as STREAM in v1.
Do not automatically rebalance RAM/STREAM classifications during live operation.
sample_loading_policy.future_extension_hint: Longer assigned samples may be opportunistically promoted to RAM in later versions if spare sample RAM exists, but this is not required for v1.

active_sample_set.purpose: playback preparation for currently assigned notes

persistence.goal: On boot, the device automatically restores the last saved playable state.
save_trigger: optional auto-save on assignment change if implemented safely outside audio path
boot_behavior: prepare assigned samples for playback according to memory policy
validation_rules: If a saved sample path no longer exists, keep booting and mark the note unassigned/error state.
Do not fail the full boot just because one file is missing.
Preserve forward compatibility using a config version field.

requirements: safe load with defaults on missing fields
When all 8 voices are active, allocate the incoming note by stealing the oldest currently active voice.
Reset the reused voice cleanly before starting new playback.

playback_model.mapping_model: one MIDI note maps to one sample path in v1

preview_behavior.purpose: browse and audition library files without assigning them first
preview_behavior.implementation: on-demand stream from SD via non-audio loader path feeding playback safely
notes: Preview playback should not require preloading the full library.
Preview path may be lower priority than assigned performance playback.

boot_sequence: start audio task on dedicated core with preallocated working memory
scan sample directory and build lightweight library index
read WAV headers for assigned samples only
classify assigned samples as RAM or STREAM according to threshold and sample RAM budget
load RAM-classified assigned samples into sample RAM pool
initialize stream states/buffers for STREAM-capable playback
signal UI that system is ready

midi_note_on: push trigger event to audio trigger queue
audio engine allocates free voice or steals oldest active voice
voice starts from frame 0 using RAM or stream source
audio mixer renders into output buffer
assignment_change: UI selects MIDI note and sample from library index
save operation persists mapping to JSON
loader prepares newly assigned sample metadata and RAM/STREAM classification
audio engine uses updated assignment only after safe handoff
library_preview: UI requests preview for library item
loader opens file and prepares temporary streaming source
playback occurs without requiring full assignment pipeline
preview stops and temporary resources are released cleanly

modules.name: LibraryIndex
modules.responsibility: Maintain lightweight list of sample files available on SD for browsing and assignment selection.

modules.name: SettingsStore
modules.responsibility: Load and save JSON configuration containing global settings and MIDI assignments.

modules.name: AssignmentManager
modules.responsibility: Manage current MIDI note to sample path mapping and validation.

modules.name: ActiveSampleRegistry
modules.responsibility: Hold fully prepared descriptors only for MIDI-assigned samples.

modules.name: SampleRamManager
modules.responsibility: Own sample RAM budget and load qualifying assigned samples into RAM.

modules.name: StreamManager
modules.responsibility: Maintain read-ahead buffers and SD-backed playback support for streamed voices and preview playback.

modules.name: TriggerQueue
modules.responsibility: Transfer playback requests safely into audio domain.

modules.name: VoicePool
modules.responsibility: Own the 8 fixed voice slots and their runtime playback state.

modules.name: VoiceAllocator
modules.responsibility: Allocate free voice or steal oldest active voice.

modules.name: AudioMixer
modules.responsibility: Mix active voices into output buffer using preprepared sources only.

modules.name: UiStateController
modules.responsibility: Drive browsing, assignment editing, save/load status, and diagnostics display.

hard_requirements: No blocking SD read in the critical audio mixing loop.
No malloc/free churn inside steady-state audio callback/task loop.
Audio engine must be able to run independently from UI activity.
Only MIDI-assigned samples participate in preload decision-making.
Saved settings and assignments must be loaded automatically at boot.
Missing assigned files must degrade gracefully rather than crash startup.
Oldest active voice stealing must be implemented deterministically.
preferred_requirements: Use explicit ownership boundaries for state.
Provide clear debug counters for memory and streaming behavior.
Make preload threshold and sample RAM budget configurable through saved settings.

debug_views: which assigned samples are RAM vs STREAM

acceptance_criteria: After reboot, saved assignments and settings are restored automatically without manual reconfiguration.
The engine supports 8 simultaneous voices under normal operation.
When a 9th trigger arrives, the oldest active voice is stolen and replaced deterministically.
Audio mixing runs on a dedicated core/task domain isolated from UI and loader work.
Only MIDI-assigned samples are deeply prepared for playback; the rest of the library remains lightweight for browsing.
Short assigned samples are loaded to RAM until sample RAM budget is exhausted; remaining assigned samples stream from SD.
UI browsing and settings operations do not interrupt steady audio playback.
System starts into a playable state automatically after boot if SD and saved config are valid enough.
non_goals_for_v1: Do not optimize for maximum theoretical polyphony above stability target.
Do not implement advanced cache promotion or eviction logic.
Do not model the full library as fully parsed playback-ready assets at boot.
Do not solve future preset architecture in this task.
